propositions: A transient GitHub git-fetch hang during throwaway clone creation causes subprocess.TimeoutExpired, which is converted to SnapshotFetchError and caught as a generic exception, resulting in a spurious LLM-Review -1 block vote.

The -1 vote removal of a change from backfill reconciliation (which pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote) makes infrastructure faults durable: a several-second network blip permanently wedges the change until manual re-trigger.

The review bot lacks distinction between retryable infrastructure faults and genuine review conclusions, routing both through the vote-bearing path when infrastructure faults should abstain and remain eligible for backfill retry.
Infrastructure timeouts (git fetch stall, network timeout, connection error) must be classified separately and handled by the existing no-vote safety path already used at the outer reconcile layer.
Posting an LLM-Review vote on an infrastructure fault violates fail-open semantics: the vote persists across retries and removes the change from the designed self-healing backfill loop.
